question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s consolidated control over the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced by repeated anti-corruption campaigns that have removed potential rivals from senior party, state, and military posts, underpins the 95.5% trader consensus that he will remain general secretary and president through the end of 2026. No successor has been elevated to the Politburo Standing Committee, age-based retirement norms were set aside after his third term, and the 21st Party Congress in 2027 is widely viewed as the venue for extending his leadership rather than a transition. Public appearances and policy continuity into mid-2026 signal stable elite alignment. Low-probability shifts could still arise from sudden health events, severe economic shocks, or unforeseen fractures in party or military institutions before the congress.
